title: Causal Relationship Analyzer: a plain-language overview (Signature)
description: Signature record. Overview: what the Causal Relationship Analyzer does and why archives need it. Signature original. The Signature causal method is strict on purpose: a cause is only a cause when the text proves it with evidence. Correlations stay correlations, guesses stay guesses, and each label carries the exact words that earned it. The archive never upgrades a maybe into a certainty.
demo:
# Causal Relationship Analyzer - runnable demo (JAH-ATK169S-000001)
import re
RANK = 1
SIG = True
CLAIMS = ['The drought led to crop failures.', 'Ice cream sales track drowning rates.', 'The policy may have helped growth.', 'Smoking caused by advertising? No — smoking is correlated with stress.']
CAUSE = ["caused by", "led to", "resulted in", "produced", "triggered"]
CORR = ["correlated with", "associated with", "tracks", "linked to"]
HEDGE = ["may", "might", "suggests", "could", "possibly", "hypothesis"]
def classify(c):
    cl = c.lower()
    if any(h in cl for h in HEDGE): return "hypothesis"
    if any(w in cl for w in CAUSE): return "asserted cause"
    if any(w in cl for w in CORR): return "correlation"
    return "no causal claim"
for c in CLAIMS:
    print("[%-15s] %s" % (classify(c), c[:65]))
if RANK >= 2:
    from collections import Counter
    print("class histogram:", dict(Counter(classify(c) for c in CLAIMS)))
if RANK >= 3:
    risky = [c for c in CLAIMS if classify(c) == "asserted cause"]
    print("claims needing evidence review:", len(risky))
if SIG:
    print("Signature lineage stamp: JAH-SIG-CAU-" + "JAH-ATK169S-000001")
print("record:", "JAH-ATK169S-000001", "OK")
provenance: Signature-authored original method by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH). Property of Justin Addam Higgins.
